renders._yaml:
- component: figure
  title: F1 per callset
  description: |-
    Each bar is the F1 score of one structural-variant callset against the truth set. It answers which callset matches the truth best.
    How to read: a taller bar means a callset that agrees with the truth. Compare it with the precision and recall in the table to see whether the gap is missed variants or false calls.
    Note: svbenchmark reports recall as the share of true variants that are not false negatives and precision as the share of test variants that are not false positives. The cited page states no cut-off for F1, so none is drawn.
    Lines and annotations: The dashed line is the median F1 score of this table, a reference computed from the rows on show (it follows the filters), not a cut-off of svbenchmark.
    Source: https://svanalyzer.readthedocs.io/en/latest/svbenchmark.html
  visu_type: bar
  dict_kwargs:
    x: label
    y: f1
    labels:
      label: Callset
      f1: F1 score
  reference_lines:
  - axis: y
    stat: median
    column: f1

- component: table
  title: Structural-variant benchmark
  description: |-
    Each row is a callset with its precision, recall and F1, and the true positives, false positives and false negatives, the caller and the truth set when the run records them. It answers the numbers behind the bars.
    How to read: a low recall with a high precision means the caller misses truth variants, and the reverse means it calls false ones.
    Source: https://svanalyzer.readthedocs.io/en/latest/svbenchmark.html
